questions.explanation: Time must be converted to seconds: 1 minute = 60 s. Distance = velocity x time. x = (25 m/s)(60 s) = 1500 meters.

questions.questionText: If an object's position-time graph is a parabola opening upwards, the object is undergoing:
questions.explanation:
A parabolic x-t graph corresponds to motion with constant acceleration.

 Opening upwards means the acceleration (which is proportional to the second derivative) is positive, indicating constant positive acceleration.

questions.questionText: A car moving at 20 m/s brakes and stops in 4 seconds. What is the magnitude of its acceleration (deceleration)?
questions.explanation:
v = v₀ + at. 0 = 20 m/s + a(4 s). 
a = -20 m/s / 4 s = -5 m/s².
 The magnitude is 5 m/s².

questions.questionText: The slope of a velocity-time graph (v-t graph) represents which physical quantity?
questions.explanation: The slope of a v-t graph is the change in velocity divided by the change in time, which defines acceleration.

questions.questionText: In a position-time graph, a steeper slope indicates:
questions.explanation: Slope represents velocity. A steeper slope (larger magnitude of slope) means the object is changing its position more rapidly, indicating a faster speed.

questions.questionText: A ball is thrown straight up. When is the magnitude of its acceleration the greatest, ignoring air resistance?
options: At the highest point of its path.
The acceleration magnitude is constant throughout the motion.
questions.explanation:
In free fall, the acceleration is due to gravity (g = 9.8 m/s²) and is directed downwards.

 This value is constant at all points in the trajectory, including the moment it is thrown and the moment it peaks.

questions.questionText: A car accelerates uniformly from 10 m/s to 30 m/s over a displacement of 80 meters. What is its acceleration?
If an object travels at a constant velocity, its average velocity over any time interval will be:
questions.explanation:
If the velocity is constant, the instantaneous velocity at any point is the same as the velocity over the entire interval.

 Thus, average velocity is equal to its instantaneous velocity.

questions.questionText: A car starts from rest and travels 100 meters in 5 seconds with uniform acceleration. What is its acceleration?
An object's velocity-time graph is a straight line with a negative slope. This indicates:
options: The object is moving in the negative direction.
The object is moving at constant velocity.
The object is moving at constant positive acceleration.
questions.explanation:
A negative slope on a v-t graph means negative acceleration. 

If the initial velocity was positive, negative acceleration means the object is decelerating (slowing down).

 (If the velocity was already negative, it would be speeding up).

questions.questionText: Which kinematic equation is most suitable for finding the final velocity (v) when initial velocity (v₀), acceleration (a), and displacement (x) are known, but time (t) is unknown?
questions.explanation: The equation v² = v₀² + 2ax is the 'time-independent' kinematic equation, directly relating final velocity to the other three variables.

questions.questionText: What is the total distance traveled by an object whose position-time graph has coordinates (t=0, x=0), (t=5s, x=10m), and (t=10s, x=0)?
questions.explanation: Total distance is the path length. The object moves 10 m from 0 to 5s, and then 10 m from 10m back to 0m. Total distance = 10 m + 10 m = 20 meters.

questions.questionText: A free-falling object is thrown downward with an initial speed of 5 m/s. After 2 seconds, what is its speed (g = 10 m/s²)?
questions.explanation:
Use v = v₀ + gt.
 v = 5 m/s + (10 m/s²)(2 s) =
 5 m/s + 20 m/s = 25 m/s.

questions.questionText: If an object’s acceleration is 3 m/s², what does this mean about its motion?
options: Its speed decreases by 3 m/s every second.
Its velocity changes by 3 m/s every second.
It takes 3 seconds to travel 1 meter.
questions.explanation:
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.

 An acceleration of 3 m/s² means the object's velocity changes by 3 m/s every second.

questions.questionText: The time it takes for an object thrown straight up to reach its maximum height is equal to the time it takes for the object to fall back from that height to the starting point, assuming no air resistance. This is due to:
options: Kinetic energy equaling zero at the peak.
questions.explanation: Because the acceleration (g) is constant and acts downwards throughout the entire motion (up and down), the symmetry of the path dictates equal times for the ascent and descent phases.

questions.questionText: A runner completes one lap (400 m) around a circular track in 50 seconds. What is her average velocity?
questions.explanation:
Average velocity = total displacement / total time. 

Since the runner ends up at the starting point, the net displacement is zero.
 Therefore, the average velocity is 0 m/s.

questions.questionText: A velocity-time graph is a horizontal straight line at v = -5 m/s. This represents motion with:
options: Increasing speed in the negative direction.
questions.explanation:
A horizontal line on a v-t graph has a zero slope, meaning zero acceleration.

 The velocity is constant and negative, indicating zero acceleration and negative velocity.

questions.questionText: A truck accelerates from rest at 2 m/s². What is its displacement after 4 seconds?
If a particle's acceleration-time graph is a straight line at a = 4 m/s², its motion is characterized by:
questions.explanation: A constant value on an a-t graph means the particle is undergoing motion with constant (uniform) acceleration.

questions.questionText: A common definition of deceleration is:
options: Acceleration that is opposite in direction to the velocity.
Velocity that is opposite in direction to the displacement.
questions.explanation: Deceleration refers to the condition where the object is slowing down, which happens when the acceleration vector is directed opposite to the velocity vector.

questions.questionText: The slope of the tangent line to a curve on a position-time graph gives the:
questions.explanation: The instantaneous rate of change of position is represented by the slope of the tangent to the curve on an x-t graph, which is the instantaneous velocity.

questions.questionText: An object in free fall dropped from a height (h) takes 4 seconds to reach the ground. From what height was it dropped (g = 10 m/s²)?
What is the maximum number of times an object moving with non-zero, constant acceleration can pass the same point?
questions.explanation:
An object with constant acceleration can only reverse direction once (when v=0).

 For example, a ball thrown up. It passes the starting point once on the way up and once on the way down. Thus, it can pass the same point a maximum of two times.

questions.questionText: If the velocity of an object is proportional to the time squared (v = kt²), its acceleration is:
questions.explanation:
Acceleration is the derivative (rate of change) of velocity with respect to time. If v = kt², then a = dv/dt = 2kt.
 The acceleration is proportional to time.

questions.questionText: A particle moves with uniform acceleration. If its initial velocity is 10 m/s and its final velocity is 30 m/s, what is its average velocity for that time interval?
questions.explanation:
For uniform acceleration, the average velocity is the arithmetic mean of the initial and final velocities.

 Average v = (v₀ + v) / 2 = (10 m/s + 30 m/s) / 2 = 20 m/s.

questions.questionText: Which of the following conditions is required for the application of the kinematic equations (v = v₀ + at, etc.)?
options: The motion must be in a curve.
The mass of the object must be known.
questions.explanation: The derivation of the standard kinematic equations is based entirely on the assumption of constant or uniform acceleration.

questions.questionText: A racing car slows down from 80 m/s to 40 m/s over a distance of 60 meters. What is the magnitude of the deceleration?
questions.explanation:
Use v² = v₀² + 2ax. (40)² = (80)² + 2a(60). 1600 = 6400 + 120a. -4800 = 120a. a = -40 m/s². 
The magnitude of the deceleration is 40 m/s².

questions.questionText: If a position-time graph shows a curve that is getting **less steep** as time increases, the object is:
questions.explanation: The steepness (slope) represents speed. A decreasing slope means the velocity magnitude is decreasing, so the object is slowing down.

questions.questionText: What is the meaning of a negative sign in a displacement value (e.g., -10 meters)?
options: The object traveled a shorter distance.
The object is moving slower than average.
The object is moving opposite to the designated positive direction.
questions.explanation: In one-dimensional motion, a negative sign on a vector quantity (displacement, velocity, acceleration) indicates a direction opposite to the one defined as positive.

questions.questionText: A body is thrown upwards. If air resistance is neglected, the time to reach maximum height is given by:
questions.explanation:
At maximum height, the final velocity (v) is 0.
 Using v = v₀ - gt: 0 = v₀ - gt, which rearranges to t = v₀ / g.

questions.questionText: A velocity-time graph is a straight line passing through the origin with a positive slope. This indicates:
options: Constant positive acceleration, starting from rest.
questions.explanation:
A straight line means constant acceleration (positive slope is positive acceleration).

 Passing through the origin (v=0 at t=0) means the object starts from rest with constant positive acceleration.

questions.questionText: If a car's speedometer reads 60 km/h, this is a measure of its:
questions.explanation: A speedometer shows the magnitude of the velocity at that precise moment, which is the instantaneous speed.

questions.questionText: A bullet is shot vertically upward and returns to the ground. If the upward journey takes 5 seconds, how long does the entire flight take (no air resistance)?
questions.explanation: Due to constant acceleration (g), the time for the upward flight equals the time for the downward flight. Total time = 5 s (up) + 5 s (down) = 10 seconds.

questions.questionText: What is the value of the instantaneous acceleration at time t = 2s for an object whose velocity is given by v(t) = 5t² - 10t?
questions.explanation:
Acceleration is the derivative of velocity: a(t) = dv/dt = 10t - 10.

->  At t = 2s, a(2) = 10(2) - 10 = 20 - 10 = 10 m/s².

questions.questionText: Which statement is true for an object that is speeding up?
options: Its velocity and acceleration must have opposite signs.
Its velocity and acceleration must have the same sign.
questions.explanation: For an object to speed up, the acceleration must be in the same direction as the velocity, meaning its velocity and acceleration vectors must have the same sign.

questions.questionText: On a velocity-time graph, a negative area under the curve indicates:
questions.explanation: Area under the v-t graph is displacement. If the velocity is negative, the object is moving in the negative direction, resulting in a negative displacement.

questions.questionText: A particle moves from x = 10 m to x = 30 m in 5 seconds. Its initial velocity is 2 m/s. What is its acceleration?
The time of flight for a vertically launched object depends only on its initial velocity and:
questions.explanation:
The time of flight (from launch to return) is given by T = 2v₀/g. 

It depends on the initial velocity (v₀) and the acceleration due to gravity (g), neglecting air resistance.

questions.questionText: If the slope of a position-time graph increases uniformly, the acceleration of the object is:
questions.explanation: Increasing slope means increasing velocity. If the slope increases *uniformly*, the rate of change of the slope (acceleration) is **constant and non-zero**.

questions.questionText: A rock is thrown straight down from a bridge with an initial velocity of 10 m/s. If it hits the water 2 seconds later, how high is the bridge (g = 10 m/s²)?
In the equation x = v₀t + (1/2)at², the term 'x' represents:
questions.explanation: In this kinematic equation, 'x' is the displacement of the object from its starting point (x₀) after time 't'.

questions.questionText: An object's velocity changes from -20 m/s to -30 m/s in 5 seconds. Its acceleration is:
The slope of an acceleration-time graph (a-t graph) represents the rate of change of acceleration, known as:
questions.explanation: The rate of change of acceleration is a specific physical quantity known as Jerk (J = da/dt).

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements is TRUE for an object undergoing uniform acceleration?
options: Its position changes linearly with time.
Its average velocity equals its instantaneous velocity.
Its velocity changes linearly with time.
questions.explanation:
Uniform acceleration means the velocity changes by the same amount in every equal time interval.

 This means the graph of velocity versus time is a straight line, and the velocity changes linearly with time (v = v₀ + at).

questions.questionText: A cyclist travels 100 meters north in 10 seconds and then 100 meters south in 10 seconds. The average speed for the entire trip is:
questions.explanation:
Average speed = Total distance / Total time.
 Total distance = 100 m + 100 m = 200 m.
 Total time = 10 s + 10 s = 20 s.

 Average speed = 200 m / 20 s = 10 m/s.

questions.questionText: The time taken for a projectile launched vertically upward to reach a height of 10 meters is 1 second (g = 10 m/s²). What was the initial launch velocity?
If a position-time graph shows an object starting at a positive position, the motion is:
options: Determined by the slope, not the intercept.
questions.explanation:
The starting position (intercept) is independent of the motion (slope). 
The direction and nature of the motion are determined by the slope of the graph (velocity).

questions.questionText: A car accelerates uniformly from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 4 seconds. How far does it travel in this time?
An object's velocity is given by v = -2 + 4t. At what time does the object change its direction of motion?
questions.explanation:
An object changes direction when its velocity momentarily becomes zero.
 Set v = 0: 0 = -2 + 4t. 4t = 2. t = 2/4 = 0.5 seconds.

questions.questionText: A free-falling object has a velocity of -15 m/s. One second later, its velocity is (g = 10 m/s²):
questions.explanation:
Use v = v₀ + at. (We take down as negative, so a = -g = -10 m/s²).

 v = -15 m/s + (-10 m/s²)(1 s) = -15 m/s - 10 m/s = -25 m/s.

questions.questionText: The term instantaneous acceleration refers to the acceleration:
options: At a specific point in time.
Equal to the change in displacement divided by time.
questions.explanation:
Instantaneous acceleration is the limiting value of the average acceleration as the time interval approaches zero; 

-> it describes the rate of velocity change at a specific moment in time.

questions.questionText: If a particle moves with constant speed but its velocity is changing, its motion is necessarily:
questions.explanation:
Velocity is a vector. If its magnitude (speed) is constant but its direction is changing, the velocity is changing, which means the path cannot be a straight line (linear).
 It must be a non-linear (curved) path.

questions.questionText: A train slows from 20 m/s to a stop with an acceleration of -4 m/s². How long does it take to stop?
questions.explanation:
Use v = v₀ + at.
 0 = 20 m/s + (-4 m/s²)t.
 4t = 20. 
t = 20 / 4 = 5 seconds.

questions.questionText: The ratio of an object's total distance traveled to the total time elapsed is the:
questions.explanation: This is the definition of average speed: total distance divided by the total time taken.

questions.questionText: An object's velocity-time graph is a downward-sloping straight line that crosses the time axis. At the point it crosses the axis, the object has:
options: Zero speed and maximum acceleration magnitude.
questions.explanation:
Crossing the time axis (v=0) means zero speed. Since the line is straight, the acceleration (slope) is constant.

 Thus, it has zero speed and constant acceleration.

questions.questionText: If an object is thrown vertically upwards with initial velocity v₀, what is the total vertical distance traveled when it returns to the launch point?
questions.explanation:
The maximum height reached is h = v₀² / 2g. The total distance traveled is twice the maximum height.

 Total Distance = 2 * (v₀² / 2g) =
 v₀² / g.

questions.questionText: A position-time graph consists of two segments: a steep positive slope followed by a less steep positive slope. This indicates:
options: Speeding up then slowing down, but always moving forward.
questions.explanation:
Both slopes are positive, meaning the object is always moving in the positive direction.

 A steep slope (fast speed) followed by a less steep slope (slower speed) means the object is speeding up then slowing down.

questions.questionText: An object starts from rest and moves for 10 seconds with an acceleration of 2 m/s². The distance traveled in the **10th second only** is:
questions.explanation:
Distance in the n-th second = (Distance in 10s) - (Distance in 9s). x(10) =
 (1/2)(2)(10)² = 100 m. x(9) = (1/2)(2)(9)² = 81 m.
 Distance in 10th second = 100 m - 81 m = 19 meters.

questions.questionText: The time required for an object dropped from rest to reach a velocity of 30 m/s is (g = 10 m/s²):
questions.explanation:
Use v = v₀ + gt. 30 m/s = 0 + (10 m/s²)t.
 t = 30 / 10 = 3.0 seconds.

questions.questionText: If the equation of motion is x(t) = 3t² - 5t + 2, the initial position (x₀) of the object is:
questions.explanation: The initial position is the position at t = 0. x(0) = 3(0)² - 5(0) + 2 = 2 meters.

questions.questionText: An object starts from rest and reaches a speed of 10 m/s. It then travels at this constant speed for 5 seconds. The total displacement is represented by the sum of the areas of a triangle and a rectangle on which graph?
questions.explanation:
Displacement is the area under the curve of a Velocity-time graph.
 The accelerating phase is a triangle, and the constant velocity phase is a rectangle.

questions.questionText: If an object's position is given by x = 5t, the object's average velocity over any time interval is:
questions.explanation: The velocity is the derivative of position: v = dx/dt = 5 m/s. Since the velocity is constant (5 m/s), the average velocity is also 5 m/s.

questions.questionText: A rocket launching vertically starts from rest and achieves a speed of 100 m/s after traveling 500 meters. What is the magnitude of its acceleration?
Which of the following describes the relationship between distance and the magnitude of displacement in one-dimensional motion?
options: Distance is always less than displacement.
Distance is always greater than displacement.
Distance is always equal to the magnitude of displacement.
Distance is greater than or equal to the magnitude of displacement.
questions.explanation:
Distance is the total path length. Displacement is the straight-line change in position.
 In all cases, the distance traveled is greater than or equal to the magnitude of the displacement (equal only if there is no change in direction).

questions.questionText: The time it takes for an object thrown straight up to return to its initial height is known as the:
questions.explanation: The total duration an object spends in the air, from launch until it returns to the original height, is called the Time of flight.

questions.questionText: If the slope of a position-time graph is negative and constant, the object is moving:
options: In the positive direction and speeding up.
In the negative direction with constant speed.
In the negative direction and slowing down.
questions.explanation:
Negative slope means negative velocity (moving in the negative direction). 

Constant slope means constant velocity (constant speed). Thus, the object is moving in the negative direction with constant speed.

questions.questionText: A particle’s velocity-time graph is a line segment from (0, 0) to (5s, 10 m/s). What is the total distance traveled?
questions.explanation:
Distance is the area of the triangle under the v-t graph.

 Area = (1/2) * base * height = (1/2) * 5 s * 10 m/s = 25 meters.

questions.questionText: The acceleration due to gravity (g) near the Earth’s surface is approximately:
questions.explanation: The standard accepted value for the acceleration due to gravity (g) is approximately 9.8 m/s².

questions.questionText: A bus slows from 20 m/s to 10 m/s in 5 seconds. What is the distance covered during this time interval?
If a particle's motion is described by the equation x = 5t³, its instantaneous velocity at t = 2s is:
questions.explanation:
Velocity is the derivative of position: v(t) = dx/dt = 15t².
 At t = 2s, v(2) = 15(2)² =
 15(4) = 60 m/s.

questions.questionText: When an object is thrown straight up, the direction of its acceleration on the way up is:
questions.explanation: The acceleration is always due to gravity, which is directed **downward** throughout the entire flight (up and down), assuming negligible air resistance.

questions.questionText: If an object moves such that its distance is always equal to the magnitude of its displacement, it must be moving:
questions.explanation: Distance equals the magnitude of displacement only if the object travels along a straight line without changing its direction.

questions.questionText: A rock is dropped from a cliff. The ratio of its velocity at t=1s to its velocity at t=3s is:
questions.explanation: Velocity in free fall is v = gt. The ratio is v₁/v₃ = (g*1s) / (g*3s) = 1:3.

questions.questionText: In a position-time graph, what indicates that the object has momentarily stopped and reversed its direction?
options: The point where the slope of the curve becomes zero.
The point where the graph crosses the time axis.
questions.explanation:
Stopping means zero velocity (slope=0). 
Reversing means the slope changes from positive to negative (or vice-versa).
 Both conditions are met at the point where the slope of the curve becomes zero (a peak or valley).

questions.questionText: A runner accelerates from 5 m/s to 10 m/s in 2 seconds. The displacement during this acceleration is:
If an object's acceleration is given by a(t) = 6t, what is the nature of its motion?
questions.explanation: Since the acceleration is changing with time (a depends on t), the motion is classified as non-uniformly accelerated motion.

questions.questionText: For a horizontally thrown object, which of the following is not a vector quantity?
questions.explanation:
Velocity, momentum, and acceleration are all vector quantities.

 Kinetic Energy (KE) is a scalar quantity, defined only by magnitude (KE = 1/2mv²).

questions.questionText: A particle moves with an initial velocity of 4 m/s and constant acceleration. Its velocity increases to 10 m/s after 2 seconds. Its acceleration is:
What is the physical meaning of the statement: 'The velocity of a particle is constant'?
options: It is in a state of free fall.
It is changing its direction of motion.
questions.explanation: Constant velocity means the rate of change of velocity is zero, which means the acceleration is zero.

questions.questionText: An object in free fall (from rest) travels a distance 'x' in time 't'. How far does it travel in time '2t'?
questions.explanation:
Distance is proportional to time squared (x = (1/2)gt²). 

If the time is doubled (2t), the distance becomes (2t)² = 4t².

 Thus, the distance is 4x.

questions.questionText: If a position-time graph has a positive slope that remains constant, which of the following is true?
questions.explanation:
Positive slope means positive velocity (v > 0).
 Constant slope means zero acceleration (a = 0).
 Thus, v > 0 and a = 0.

questions.questionText: A projectile is thrown upwards with v₀. What is the time required to reach a height of h, given the kinematic equation h = v₀t - (1/2)gt²?
options: Given by a quadratic equation (two possible times).
questions.explanation:
The equation is a quadratic in 't'. 
Since the projectile passes through height 'h' once on the way up and once on the way down, there are generally two possible times (roots) for any height less than the maximum height.

questions.questionText: The slope of the line connecting two points on a curved position-time graph represents the:
options: Instantaneous velocity at the start point.
Average velocity between the two points.
Average acceleration between the two points.
questions.explanation:
The line connecting two points is a secant line. 
Its slope (change in x / change in t) represents the average velocity over that interval.

questions.questionText: A truck's acceleration is -3 m/s². If its initial velocity is -15 m/s, the truck is:
questions.explanation:
Both velocity and acceleration are negative (pointing in the same, negative direction). 
When velocity and acceleration have the same sign, the object is speeding up.

questions.questionText: If a particle's position is x(t) = 4t + 5, what is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Velocity v(t) = dx/dt = 4. Acceleration a(t) = dv/dt = 0. The acceleration is 0 m/s².

questions.questionText: The time a ball thrown straight up spends above the halfway point (h/2) of its maximum height (h) compared to the time spent below it is:
questions.explanation:
Due to constant deceleration (gravity), the object is moving faster at the lower half of its path and slower at the upper half.

 Therefore, the time spent above the halfway point is greater than the time spent below it.

questions.questionText: An object's velocity-time graph is a rectangle above the time axis. The height is 10 m/s and the base is 5 s. The acceleration is:
questions.explanation:
A rectangular shape means the velocity is constant (v = 10 m/s).

 Since the velocity is constant, the acceleration (slope) is 0 m/s².

questions.questionText: A particle moves with an initial velocity of 2 m/s and uniform acceleration of 2 m/s². What is its displacement after 4 seconds?
What is the magnitude of the displacement of a particle that moves 20 meters East and then 5 meters West?
questions.explanation: Displacement = 20 m (East) - 5 m (West) = 15 meters East.

questions.questionText: If an object is launched vertically upward, the direction of its velocity at the very top of its flight is:
options: The velocity is zero at the top.
questions.explanation:
At the highest point, the object momentarily reverses its direction.

 Its instantaneous velocity at that precise moment is zero.

questions.questionText: The area under an acceleration-time graph (a-t graph) represents:
questions.explanation:
Area = acceleration x time. (m/s²) * s = m/s.
 This unit corresponds to change in velocity ( v = a * t).

questions.questionText: A car accelerates from 5 m/s to 15 m/s in 5 seconds. Its acceleration is:
If an object is moving in the negative direction and speeding up, its position-time graph would have a slope that is:
options: Negative and increasing in magnitude (getting steeper).
Negative and decreasing in magnitude (getting flatter).
questions.explanation:
Moving in the negative direction means the slope is negative.
 Speeding up means the speed (magnitude of slope) is increasing. 
Thus, the slope is negative and increasing in magnitude (getting steeper).

questions.questionText: A ball is thrown up and takes 3 seconds to reach the peak. What was the initial velocity (g = 10 m/s²)?
questions.explanation:
At the peak, v = 0.
 Use v = v₀ - gt. 0 =
 v₀ - (10 m/s²)(3 s). v₀ = 30 m/s.

questions.questionText: For two objects moving with the same constant acceleration, which factor primarily determines which one travels further?
options: Their initial velocity and time/distance over which they accelerate.
questions.explanation:
Given the same acceleration (a), the distance (x) is determined by the term v₀t and t² (or v² - v₀²).

 Both initial velocity and the duration/distance of acceleration are critical.

questions.questionText: The equation v = v₀ + at is valid only when:
questions.explanation: Like all kinematic equations, v = v₀ + at is derived based on the premise of uniform (constant) acceleration.

questions.questionText: A car accelerates uniformly from 10 m/s. If it travels 100 meters in 5 seconds, its acceleration is:
What is the physical meaning of a velocity-time graph that is a horizontal line at v = 0 m/s?
options: The object is moving at constant velocity.
questions.explanation: A horizontal line at v=0 means the velocity is zero and remains zero; the object is at rest.

questions.questionText: In free fall, the distance traveled by a body is proportional to the:
questions.explanation:
Starting from rest (v₀=0), the displacement is x = (1/2)gt².

 Since g is constant, x is proportional to the square of the time elapsed (t²).

questions.questionText: An object's velocity changes from 5 m/s to 15 m/s in 2 seconds. The distance covered in this time is:
A position-time graph has a negative slope that is getting flatter (magnitude decreasing) as time increases. The object is:
questions.explanation:
Negative slope means moving backward.
 Getting flatter means the speed (magnitude of slope) is decreasing.
 Thus, the object is moving backward and slowing down (decelerating).

questions.questionText: The time it takes for a ball thrown upwards with initial velocity v₀ to reach its maximum height is:
questions.explanation:
The time to peak is t = v₀/g.
 Since g is constant, the time is directly proportional to the initial velocity (v₀).

questions.questionText: Which of the following must be true for a body to be in uniform motion?
questions.explanation:
Uniform motion means constant velocity. Constant velocity means there is no change in velocity, so the acceleration must equal zero.
 If it is in a straight line, the final velocity must equal the initial velocity, making this also correct, but a=0 is the defining characteristic of uniform velocity.

questions.questionText: A particle moves from x = 5 m to x = -5 m in 2 seconds. Its average velocity is:
questions.explanation:
Average velocity = Displacement / Time.
 Displacement = Final x - Initial x = -5 m - 5 m = -10 m.
 Average v = -10 m / 2 s = -5 m/s.

questions.questionText: An object in free fall has a speed of 10 m/s at a certain height. What is its speed at the same height on its way back down?
questions.explanation: Due to the symmetry of free fall motion (constant g), the object's speed at any given height on the way up is equal to its speed at the same height on the way down.

questions.questionText: If the acceleration of a particle is constant and non-zero, its velocity-time graph is a:
options: Straight line with a non-zero slope.
questions.explanation:
Constant acceleration means a constant slope on the v-t graph.

 A non-zero, constant slope is a straight line with a non-zero slope.

questions.questionText: A ball is thrown up with a speed of 30 m/s. What is its maximum height (g = 10 m/s²)?
If an object's position-time graph is a perfect semi-circle, its motion is:
questions.explanation:
A circular curve is not a parabola, so the rate of change of the slope (acceleration) is not constant.
 The motion is non-uniformly accelerated motion.

questions.questionText: The maximum velocity reached by an object starting from rest and accelerating uniformly for 5 seconds over a distance of 100 meters is:
Which of the following is an example of an object moving with a non-zero, constant acceleration?
options: car driving on a straight road at a steady 60 km/h.
feather falling in a perfect vacuum.
train speeding up from 0 to 100 km/h in 10 seconds.
person running a fixed distance in a fixed time.
questions.explanation: A feather falling in a vacuum is subject only to gravity, which provides a constant, non-zero acceleration (g).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Force is a vector quantity because it has both magnitude and direction.

questions.questionText: Newton's First Law states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by:
questions.explanation: Newton’s First Law (Law of Inertia) states that an object will remain at rest or move uniformly unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.

questions.questionText: A 10 kg object is pushed with a force of 50 N. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Using Newton’s Second Law, F = ma ⇒ a = F/m = 50 / 10 = 5 m/s².

questions.questionText: Which force opposes motion when a block slides on a horizontal surface?
questions.explanation: Frictional force always acts opposite to the motion of an object on a surface.

questions.questionText: Work done when a 20 N force moves an object 5 m in the direction of the force is:
questions.explanation: Work = Force × Distance = 20 × 5 = 100 J.

questions.questionText: The kinetic energy of a 2 kg object moving with velocity 3 m/s is:
questions.explanation: Kinetic Energy = ½ mv² = ½ × 2 × 3² = 9 J.

questions.questionText: Potential energy depends on:
questions.explanation: Potential energy = mgh, depends on mass, gravitational acceleration, and height.

questions.questionText: Power is defined as the rate at which:
questions.explanation: Power = Work / Time. It is the rate at which work is done.

questions.questionText: If a car does 2000 J of work in 10 seconds, its power output is:
questions.explanation: Power = Work / Time = 2000 / 10 = 200 W.

questions.questionText: A force of 10 N acts on a 5 kg object. If it moves 2 m in the direction of the force, work done is:
questions.explanation: Work = Force × Distance = 10 × 2 = 20 J.

questions.questionText: The SI unit of work is:
questions.explanation: Work is measured in Joules (J). 1 J = 1 N·m.

questions.questionText: A 5 kg mass is lifted 2 m vertically. What is its gravitational potential energy? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Potential Energy = mgh = 5 × 10 × 2 = 100 J.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Work is scalar; it has magnitude only, no direction.

questions.questionText: The force required to accelerate a 4 kg object at 3 m/s² is:
A car moves at constant velocity. The net force acting on it is:
questions.explanation: When velocity is constant, net force = 0 according to Newton's First Law.

questions.questionText: If friction is neglected, an object sliding down an incline gains energy in the form of:
questions.explanation: Potential energy converts to kinetic energy as the object slides down.

questions.questionText: A force acts at an angle of 60° to the displacement. The work done is given by:
questions.explanation: Work done W = Fd cosθ, where θ is the angle between force and displacement.

questions.questionText: The rate at which kinetic energy changes is called:
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work or rate of energy transfer.

questions.questionText: A 2 kg object moving at 4 m/s has kinetic energy:
If no net work is done on an object, its kinetic energy:
questions.explanation: Work-energy theorem: if net work = 0, kinetic energy does not change.

questions.questionText: A 3 kg object is lifted 5 m vertically. The work done against gravity is:
Which of the following best describes Newton's Third Law?
options: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
Objects at rest stay at rest
questions.explanation: Newton’s Third Law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

questions.questionText: The frictional force depends on:
options: Normal force and coefficient of friction
questions.explanation: Frictional force = μ × N, where μ is coefficient of friction and N is normal force.

questions.questionText: The work done by a force of 50 N at 90° to displacement of 2 m is:
questions.explanation: Work = F × d × cosθ = 50 × 2 × cos90° = 0 J.

questions.questionText: A 2 kg object moving with 6 m/s has kinetic energy:
The gravitational potential energy of an object depends on:
questions.explanation: Potential energy = mgh, depends on mass, gravitational acceleration, and height.

questions.questionText: If a car's velocity doubles, its kinetic energy:
questions.explanation: KE = ½ mv²; doubling velocity increases KE by 2² = 4 times.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a type of friction?
questions.explanation: Gravitational force is not a type of friction.

questions.questionText: A 10 N force moves an object 3 m at 0° to the force. Work done is:
Power is measured in which SI unit?
questions.explanation: Power is measured in Watts (W).

questions.questionText: The net work done on an object is equal to:
questions.explanation: According to the work-energy theorem, net work = change in kinetic energy.

questions.questionText: A block is at rest on a horizontal surface. Which friction acts on it?
questions.explanation: Static friction prevents a stationary object from moving.

questions.questionText: A 5 kg object slides down a frictionless slope of 4 m height. Its speed at bottom is:
Which of the following statements is correct about work?
questions.explanation: Work is negative when force and displacement are in opposite directions.

questions.questionText: An object of mass 3 kg has kinetic energy 24 J. Its speed is:
A 2 kg mass is lifted 3 m in 2 s. Its power output is:
questions.explanation: Work = mgh = 2×10×3=60 J, Power = Work/Time = 60/3 = 20 W.

questions.questionText: Friction always acts:
questions.explanation: Friction opposes relative motion between surfaces.

questions.questionText: The kinetic energy of an object is zero. Its velocity is:
questions.explanation: KE = ½ mv² = 0 ⇒ velocity v = 0.

questions.questionText: Which quantity is both scalar and can be negative?
questions.explanation: Work is scalar and can be negative if force and displacement are opposite.

questions.questionText: An object moves in a circle at constant speed. The work done by centripetal force is:
questions.explanation: Centripetal force is perpendicular to displacement ⇒ work done = 0.

questions.questionText: A 4 kg object is pulled by a 12 N force over 3 m at 0° to the force. Work done is:
If the velocity of an object triples, its kinetic energy:
questions.explanation: KE = ½ mv²; tripling velocity increases KE by 3² = 9 times.

questions.questionText: Which law explains why a rocket moves forward when gases are expelled backward?
questions.explanation: Newton’s Third Law: action (gas backward) produces equal and opposite reaction (rocket forward).

questions.questionText: An object is pushed horizontally on a rough surface with a force of 20 N, friction is 5 N. Net work done over 4 m is:
questions.explanation: Net force = 20-5=15 N; Work = F × d = 15 × 4 = 60 J.

questions.questionText: A car of mass 1000 kg accelerates at 2 m/s². The force applied is:
Which type of friction allows a wheel to roll without slipping?
questions.explanation: Rolling friction acts on rolling objects, usually less than sliding friction.

questions.questionText: A 5 kg object is lifted 8 m vertically. Work done against gravity is:
Power is defined as:
questions.explanation: Power = Work done / Time taken.

questions.questionText: An object of mass 2 kg has KE = 50 J. Its velocity is:
Which of the following is scalar?
questions.explanation: Work is a scalar quantity; others are vectors.

questions.questionText: A block of 3 kg moves up a slope with friction 6 N over 4 m. Applied force 18 N. Net work done is:
questions.explanation: Net force = 18-6=12 N; Work = F × d = 12 × 3 = 36 J.

questions.questionText: An object is at rest. Which force must be overcome to move it?
questions.explanation: Static friction resists initiation of motion.

questions.questionText: A 10 N force acts on a 2 kg object for 5 s. Impulse delivered is:
questions.explanation: Impulse = Force × Time = 10 × 5 = 50 Ns.

questions.questionText: If work done is zero, which of the following must be true?
questions.explanation: Work = F × d × cosθ = 0 if displacement = 0 or force ⊥ displacement.

questions.questionText: Gravitational potential energy is maximum at:
questions.explanation: Potential energy = mgh; maximum at highest vertical position.

questions.questionText: An object moves on a horizontal surface with constant speed. Net work done is:
questions.explanation: No acceleration ⇒ net force = 0 ⇒ net work = 0.

questions.questionText: The force which opposes relative motion is called:
questions.explanation: Friction opposes relative motion between surfaces.

questions.questionText: An object is moving in a circle at constant speed. The centripetal work is:
questions.explanation: Centripetal force is perpendicular to displacement, so work = 0.

questions.questionText: Power output of a machine is 100 W doing 200 J work. Time taken is:
questions.explanation: Power = Work / Time ⇒ 100 = 200 / t ⇒ t = 2 s.

questions.questionText: An object of mass 2 kg is moving with 3 m/s. Its kinetic energy is:
questions.explanation: KE = ½ mv² = 0.5 × 2 × 3² = 9 J.

questions.questionText: A 50 N force moves an object 10 m at 30° to the horizontal. Work done is:
questions.explanation: Work = F × d × cosθ = 50 × 10 × cos30° ≈ 433 J.

questions.questionText: The law that states 'Force = mass × acceleration' is:
questions.explanation: Newton’s Second Law: F = ma.

questions.questionText: A 3 kg block is pulled across a rough surface with friction 4 N over 5 m. Applied force 14 N. Net work done is:
questions.explanation: Net force = 14-4=10 N; Work = F × d = 10 × 4.5 = 45 J.

questions.questionText: A body falls freely from 20 m height. Its velocity just before hitting ground is (g=10 m/s²):
Work done by gravity on a freely falling object is:
questions.explanation: Force of gravity and displacement are in same direction ⇒ positive work.

questions.questionText: If an object moves at constant velocity, net force acting on it is:
questions.explanation: Newton’s First Law: constant velocity ⇒ net force = 0.

questions.questionText: The friction that acts on a stationary object is called:
questions.explanation: Static friction opposes initiation of motion.

questions.questionText: Potential energy of a body of mass 5 kg at height 10 m is (g=10 m/s²):
Kinetic energy of a 2 kg body moving at 5 m/s is:
A machine does 200 J of work in 10 s. Its power is:
questions.explanation: Power = Work / Time = 200 / 10 = 20 W.

questions.questionText: Force of friction is always directed:
questions.explanation: Friction opposes relative motion.

questions.questionText: The net work done on an object moving in a circle at constant speed is:
questions.explanation: Centripetal force is perpendicular to displacement ⇒ work = 0.

questions.questionText: An object of mass 10 kg is accelerated at 3 m/s². Force applied is:
The rate of doing work is called:
questions.explanation: Power = Work / Time.

questions.questionText: An object is raised to a height of 15 m. Its potential energy increases by 300 J. Mass of object is:
Work done by a force perpendicular to displacement is:
questions.explanation: Work = F × d × cos90° = 0.

questions.questionText: A car of mass 500 kg moves with velocity 10 m/s. Its kinetic energy is:
Which friction is usually smallest in magnitude?
questions.explanation: Rolling friction < sliding (kinetic) < static friction.

questions.questionText: If net work on a body is zero, its kinetic energy:
questions.explanation: Work-energy theorem: W_net = ΔKE ⇒ ΔKE = 0 ⇒ KE constant.

questions.questionText: A 2 kg body is moving at 6 m/s. Its momentum is:
questions.explanation: Momentum = m × v = 2 × 6 = 12 kg·m/s.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best defines force?
options: push or pull on an object
The work done per unit time
questions.explanation: Force is any interaction that changes the motion of an object; it is a push or pull.

questions.questionText: Newton’s First Law of Motion is also called:
questions.explanation: First Law states that a body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true for Newton’s Third Law?
options: Action and reaction forces act on the same body
Action and reaction forces act on different bodies
questions.explanation: Action and reaction forces are equal and opposite but act on different bodies.

questions.questionText: Static friction differs from kinetic friction because:
options: It is generally greater than kinetic friction
questions.explanation: Static friction prevents motion initially and is usually greater than kinetic friction.

questions.questionText: Work is said to be done when:
options: An object moves under the action of a force
An object moves with constant speed
questions.explanation: Work occurs when a force causes displacement of an object in the direction of the force.

questions.questionText: Potential energy depends on:
questions.explanation: PE = mgh; it depends on mass, height, and gravitational acceleration.

questions.questionText: Kinetic energy depends on:
questions.explanation: KE = ½ mv²; it depends on both mass and speed of the object.

questions.questionText: The principle of conservation of energy states:
questions.explanation: Energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only change forms.

questions.questionText: Power is defined as:
questions.explanation: Power = Work / Time; it measures the rate of doing work.

questions.questionText: Unit of work in SI system is:
questions.explanation: Work is measured in Joules (J); 1 J = 1 N·m.

questions.questionText: Unit of power in SI system is:
questions.explanation: Power is measured in Watts (W); 1 W = 1 J/s.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Force has both magnitude and direction, hence it is a vector.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Energy has magnitude only, so it is a scalar.

questions.questionText: An object moving with constant speed in a straight line has:
questions.explanation: Constant speed and straight path ⇒ acceleration = 0.

questions.questionText: The work done by friction is generally:
questions.explanation: Friction opposes motion, so work done by friction is negative.

questions.questionText: A body has maximum potential energy at:
questions.explanation: PE = mgh; highest point gives maximum height ⇒ maximum PE.

questions.questionText: Kinetic energy is maximum when:
questions.explanation: KE = ½ mv²; KE increases with speed; maximum speed ⇒ maximum KE.

questions.questionText: Mechanical energy of a system is the sum of:
questions.explanation: Mechanical energy = PE + KE.

questions.questionText: A body’s energy can change from kinetic to potential due to:
questions.explanation: Gravity can convert kinetic energy into potential energy and vice versa.

questions.questionText: Power can be increased by:
options: Increasing work done or decreasing time
questions.explanation: Power = Work / Time; increasing work or decreasing time increases power.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best defines a simple machine?
options: device that reduces human effort by changing force or direction
complex combination of gears and motors
questions.explanation: A simple machine is a mechanical device that helps reduce effort by changing the magnitude or direction of force.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a type of simple machine?
questions.explanation: Generator is not a simple machine; it converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.

questions.questionText: The main purpose of a simple machine is to:
options: Increase force, change direction of force, or increase speed of movement
Reduce the mass of an object
questions.explanation: Simple machines help make work easier by increasing force, changing its direction, or increasing speed.

questions.questionText: Which type of lever has the fulcrum between the effort and load?
questions.explanation: In a first-class lever, the fulcrum is in the middle, with effort on one side and load on the other.

questions.questionText: A wheelbarrow is an example of which class of lever?
questions.explanation: In a second-class lever, the load is between the fulcrum and effort; a wheelbarrow demonstrates this.

questions.questionText: In which class of lever is the effort between the fulcrum and the load?
questions.explanation: Third-class levers have effort applied between the fulcrum and load, e.g., a pair of tongs.

questions.questionText: An inclined plane helps to:
options: Lift a load with less effort
questions.explanation: An inclined plane allows lifting a heavy object by applying smaller force over a longer distance.

questions.questionText: Which simple machine consists of a rope over a wheel?
questions.explanation: A pulley uses a wheel and rope to change the direction or magnitude of force.

questions.questionText: A screw is essentially a modified form of:
questions.explanation: A screw is a spiral inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder.

questions.questionText: A wedge helps to:
questions.explanation: A wedge converts force applied on its blunt end into forces perpendicular to its sloping sides to split objects.

questions.questionText: Mechanical advantage (MA) is defined as:
options: Distance moved by effort divided by distance moved by load
questions.explanation: MA = Load / Effort; it shows how much a machine amplifies the input force.

questions.questionText: Velocity ratio (VR) is defined as:
options: Distance moved by effort divided by distance moved by load
questions.explanation: VR = Distance moved by effort / Distance moved by load; it shows movement amplification.

questions.questionText: Efficiency of a machine is given by:
questions.explanation: Efficiency (%) = (MA / VR) × 100; it measures how effectively a machine converts input to output.

questions.questionText: Which of the following increases mechanical advantage?
questions.explanation: Longer lever arms increase the mechanical advantage by reducing the effort needed to move a load.

questions.questionText: Simple machines found at home include:
questions.explanation: Door handles (levers), knives (wedges), and pulleys are common simple machines at home.

questions.questionText: Simple machines at the workplace are often used to:
questions.explanation: Machines at the workplace reduce human effort in lifting, moving, or cutting tasks.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a compound machine?
questions.explanation: A wheelbarrow combines lever and wheel & axle, making it a compound machine.

questions.questionText: The purpose of a pulley system is to:
options: Change the direction of force and reduce effort
questions.explanation: A pulley changes direction of applied force and can reduce effort when multiple pulleys are used.

questions.questionText: Which is true about friction and efficiency of machines?
questions.explanation: Friction opposes motion and reduces the useful output, lowering efficiency.

questions.questionText: Which simple machine is used to hold objects together, like nails or clamps?
questions.explanation: Screws convert rotational motion into linear force to hold objects together.

questions.questionText: A lever can be classified based on the relative positions of fulcrum, load, and effort. Which class has the fulcrum at one end and the load at the other?
questions.explanation: In a second-class lever, the fulcrum is at one end, load at the other, and effort in between.

questions.questionText: Which simple machine is used to lift water from wells?
questions.explanation: Wheel and axle are often used in traditional well systems to lift buckets of water.

questions.questionText: The main advantage of using a ramp instead of lifting an object vertically is:
options: Reduced effort over a longer distance
questions.explanation: An inclined plane allows lifting a load with less effort by increasing the distance over which the force is applied.

questions.questionText: A wedge is essentially used to:
questions.explanation: A wedge converts force applied on its blunt end into forces that split or cut objects.

questions.questionText: The mechanical advantage of a machine is:
options: The ratio of load to effort
The ratio of effort to load
The distance moved by effort divided by distance moved by load
The ratio of input energy to output energy
questions.explanation: Mechanical advantage (MA) = Load / Effort, showing how much the machine amplifies force.

questions.questionText: Velocity ratio is a measure of:
questions.explanation: Velocity ratio (VR) = Distance moved by effort / Distance moved by load; it shows distance amplification.

questions.questionText: Efficiency of a machine is expressed as:
questions.explanation: Efficiency (%) = (MA / VR) × 100; it indicates how effectively input energy is converted to useful work.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a practical example of a lever at home?
questions.explanation: A seesaw is a first-class lever commonly found in playgrounds and at home.

questions.questionText: A crane uses pulleys mainly to:
options: Change the direction of force and reduce effort
questions.explanation: Cranes use pulley systems to lift heavy loads with less effort by changing force direction.

questions.questionText: A doorstop is an example of which simple machine?
questions.explanation: A wedge, such as a doorstop, holds the door in place by converting applied force into perpendicular forces.

questions.questionText: Simple machines in the workplace reduce:
questions.explanation: Machines at work help reduce the human effort needed for lifting, moving, or cutting.

questions.questionText: Which simple machine converts rotational motion into linear motion?
questions.explanation: A screw converts rotational motion into linear motion along its threads.

questions.questionText: The primary function of a wheel and axle is to:
questions.explanation: Wheel and axle reduce the effort needed to move or lift objects, making work easier.

questions.questionText: A pair of scissors is an example of:
questions.explanation: Scissors combine two levers and two wedges, making them a compound machine.

questions.questionText: A hammer used to pull nails demonstrates:
questions.explanation: The fulcrum is at the end (claw), effort applied at the handle, and load is the nail – a first-class lever.

questions.questionText: Which simple machine can be used to split wood?
questions.explanation: An axe or wedge converts force into lateral splitting force.

questions.questionText: Which factor decreases the efficiency of a machine?
questions.explanation: Friction opposes motion, wasting energy and reducing efficiency.

questions.questionText: A pulley with multiple wheels to reduce effort is called:
questions.explanation: Compound pulleys (block and tackle) reduce effort by distributing load across multiple pulleys.

questions.questionText: Which of the following increases the mechanical advantage of a lever?
questions.explanation: A longer effort arm increases the mechanical advantage, reducing the effort needed to lift the load.

questions.questionText: A knife blade is an example of which simple machine?
questions.explanation: A knife is a wedge, concentrating force on a small area to cut material efficiently.

questions.questionText: A lever has a load of 200 N and effort of 50 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
questions.explanation: Mechanical Advantage (MA) = Load / Effort = 200 / 50 = 4.

questions.questionText: A pulley lifts a load of 500 N using an effort of 100 N. What is the MA?
questions.explanation: MA = Load / Effort = 500 / 100 = 5.
